# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

I read the code only. Bash was denied, so I used file reads, which was enough for a read-only audit. The project is Next.js App Router. I sampled all 5 routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog` and `/thank-you`. I took `geo.config.json` as the stated goal: allow AI search crawlers, block training crawlers.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

The basics are mostly in place: the pages are server-rendered and linked from the nav, and `robots.txt` matches your policy. Four things cost points: the sitemap isn't announced in `robots.txt`, `<html>` has no `lang`, `/pricing` is marked `noindex` while sitemap-listed, and `/blog` loads its content only in the browser. There are no unknowns that change the score. The score is read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point robots.txt at your sitemap (GEO-011)
- **Why it matters:** crawlers use the `Sitemap:` line to find your list of pages. Without it, they have to guess where the list is.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5`
- **What the code says:** the file has only `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /`, `User-agent: GPTBot` and `Disallow: /`. It has no `Sitemap:` line, although `public/sitemap.xml` exists.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80.

### 2. Set the page language and give /blog its own title and description (GEO-012)
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines which language the site is in. `/blog` currently shows the same title and description as the home page.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`, and `app/blog/page.tsx`, which has no metadata. It can't export any, because it is a client component.
- **What the code says:** `<html>` has no attribute at all. `/blog` inherits `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'` from the layout.
- **Size:** Small. Use `<html lang="en">`. For the blog, move the page body into a client child component and export `metadata` from a server `page.tsx`. That change also fixes item 3 on `/blog`.
- **Score after this:** 80 with both changes. With `lang` alone, 18 ÷ 23 = 78.

### 3. Add canonicals to /docs and /blog (GEO-015)
- **Why it matters:** a canonical link names the main address of a page, so duplicate addresses don't confuse search engines.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };` has no `alternates.canonical`. `/blog` has no metadata at all.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 17.5 ÷ 23 = 76.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and small | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, valid and tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed per policy | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows `*`. Only `GPTBot`, a training crawler, is blocked, which matches your policy. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. `/pricing` is in the sitemap and the nav. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your origin | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/pricing` are fine. `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx` have none. 2 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:7-9` fetches posts inside `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/posts')…`. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No `application/ld+json` found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap valid and discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. Site-wide. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` `<html>` has no `lang`, so every route is affected. `/blog` also inherits the default metadata. |
| GEO-016 | Routes linked by server-rendered links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` has `<a href>` links to `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs` and `/blog`. `/thank-you` is deliberately unlinked. |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:15` uses only the scoped `data-nosnippet`. No middleware or `headers()` in the repo. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | I read `app/layout.tsx` and the 5 pages. There are no images, and every link has text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (informational) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. It isn't scored. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (informational) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app project. It isn't scored. |

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`. It compares real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Real status codes and headers:** whether pages answer 200, and any `X-Robots-Tag` set outside the repo (GEO-014, GEO-017). A live scan would confirm these.
- **GEO-017 extras:** `/api/posts` doesn't exist in this repo, so the blog's content source is unknown.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, which `geo.config.json` says.
- `/thank-you` is intentionally `noindex` and left out of the sitemap and nav, so I didn't count it against you.
- I assumed `/pricing` being `noindex` is a mistake, because it's in your sitemap and nav. If it is intentional, remove it from both and the problem goes away.
- Blocking `GPTBot` is your training-crawler choice (`trainingCrawlers: "block"`). It isn't scored.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
